In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
passive activation of neck proprioceptive afferents does not influence the discharge patterns of vestibular nuclei neurons.
neck proprioceptive input does not influence the discharge patterns of PVP and VO vestibular neurons during active gaze shifts.
neck proprioception does not influence the discharges of vestibular neurons during active head movements, and thus, does not play a role in the attenuation of vestibular responses during gaze shifts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the passive head rotation did not influence the discharge patterns of vestibular neurons.
the passive activation of neck proprioceptive input does not influence the discharge patterns of vestibular nuclei neurons.
the neck motor command has no significant influence on the response properties of the neurons we recorded, but that neck proprioception does not influence vestibular neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
neck proprioceptive inputs do not contribute to the differential processing of vestibulo-ocular information that occurs during voluntary gaze shifts.
neck proprioceptive inputs are not sufficient to explain the attenuation of vestibular neuron discharges during active gaze shifts.
the influence of neck proprioception on the responses of vestibulo-collic neurons is not sufficient to account for the observed attenuation of their responses during voluntary gaze shifts.
